children: Nvidia
received an upgrade following CEO Jensen Huang's rapid reinstatement, while Alphabet
saw its rating lifted after a significant price decline brought shares to technical support levels. On the downgrade side, Sandisk
faces concerns about a potential NAND cycle peak and intensifying Chinese competition, while Microsoft
drew a sell rating as analysts warn that rising depreciation from AI infrastructure spending will erode the company's historically strong margins.
Upgrades
Nvidia
Upgrade to Buy by

. The analyst cites Jensen Huang's return as CEO and attractive valuation at roughly 9x fiscal 2028 forward earnings as key reasons for the upgrade, noting that NVDA's full-stack strategy deepens ecosystem integration across AI factories, agents, and robotics.

"The ecosystem Jensen has built around Nvidia—and continues to build—is nothing short of exceptional...I think now, assuming Jensen remains at the helm, Nvidia's updated fiscal 2028 outlook, with growth expectations raised from 70% to 75%, provides a reasonable foundation for valuation assessment. In case those growth assumptions hold, Nvidia trades at roughly 9x fiscal 2028 forward earnings."
Alphabet
Upgrade Sell to Hold by

. The analyst upgraded shares after the stock fell nearly 35% from its May highs, reaching technical support around $260, though fundamental concerns about AI disruption to Google Search and negative free cash flows remain.

"Alphabet is now almost 35% below its all-time highs reached in May—it lost more than a third of its value already. Technically, it reached the support on the 5Y chart right around $260. Thus, it makes sense to temporarily upgrade Alphabet to a Hold (Neutral)."
Downgrades
Sandisk
Downgrade to Hold by

. The analyst warns that NAND may be nearing a cyclical peak as Chinese cloud providers cut enterprise SSD orders and consumer demand weakens, while competition from Chinese chipmaker YMTC threatens to pressure global NAND pricing.

"The NAND memory segment is starting to face headwinds that suggest we may be closer to the cyclical peak. Chinese cloud service providers (CSPs) are cutting down their enterprise SSD orders, as they aren't monetizing AI demand as well to justify forking out higher-priced memory. ... I expect this to accelerate a downturn in the NAND cycle and structurally weaken the market shares position of players such as Sandisk."
Microsoft

Downgrade Hold to Sell by Elina Selianska. The analyst argues that Microsoft's transformation from a zero-production-cost software business to cloud and AI infrastructure will permanently compress margins as depreciation from massive capital spending begins flowing through the income statement.

"Investors still value Microsoft by the standards of an old software giant with zero production cost, while the business is already transforming into infrastructure with an endless cycle of chip replacement and a margin sliding down. When such a restructuring of the business is layered on the tough policy of the Fed, geopolitics, and problems with government debt, holding the capitalization at $3.7 trillion on stubbornness alone won't work."
